title: `PrimitiveMesh.flip_faces` does not work for non-indexed meshes
body:
### Tested versions

v4.7.stable.arch_linux [5b4e0cb0f]

### System information

Godot v4.7.stable (5b4e0cb0f) - Arch Linux #1 SMP PREEMPT_DYNAMIC Fri, 26 Jun 2026 07:16:33 +0000 on X11 - X11 display driver, Multi-window, 1 monitor - Vulkan (Forward+) - dedicated AMD Radeon RX 7600 (RADV NAVI33) - 13th Gen Intel(R) Core(TM) i7-13700K (24 threads) - 31.10 GiB memory - PulseAudio (44100 Hz, Stereo/mono)

### Issue description

The flag `flip_faces` in `PrimitiveMesh` does nothing if the vertices are not indexed.

The code in question is clearly written to only work on indexed meshes:

https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/5902d3f370db5905444a01139722a40cb29bb1c4/scene/resources/3d/primitive_meshes.cpp#L81-L103

If no index array is present, it should be altered to flip the vertex order in all the other arrays (VERTEX, UV, ...).

Alternatively, the code should emit a warning that `flip_faces` is being ignored, and a note should be added to the documentation.

Incidentally, it also won't work if no normals are present, even if there is an index array.

### Steps to reproduce

- Create a custom subclass of `PrimitiveMesh` that does not use an index array. In my case, this is to produce flat shading.
- Toggle "Flip Faces" and watch it do nothing, instead of turning the mesh inside out.

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

n/a
